title: Glimpse: Geometry Learning of Multi-scale Structural Priors for 3D Pose Estimation
claim: Local sampling around an ambiguous occluded joint gives wrong predictions; adding limb-guided context across occlusions yields accurate poses.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right: photo, two stacked context panels, two outcome boxes
description: The left panel is a real photo of a person sitting on the floor in a motion-capture room. A colored skeleton is overlaid on the person and a red-yellow star marks an ambiguous joint. The caption reads "Occlusion & Depth Ambiguity". The middle column has a cyan background and two stacked heatmap-style panels. The top panel, "Joint-level Context", shows local sampling around the ambiguous joint, with white arrows pointing to nearby yellow stars. The bottom panel, "Limb-level Context", shows limb-guided sampling across occlusions, with cyan sampling points along green limbs and arrows pointing along them. Each middle panel leads by arrow to a dashed box on the right that holds a 3D skeleton plot. The top arrow carries a red X, and the plot shows the prediction (black star) far from the ground truth (pink star). The bottom plot shows the prediction matching the ground truth. The eye goes first to the photo, then to the red X and the contrast between the two skeleton plots.
caption: Illustration of the structured sampling strategy. Our
abstract: Monocular 3D human pose estimation is fundamentally challenged by severe occlusion and inherent depth ambiguity. To address this, we propose Glimpse, a framework that learns robust 3D poses by explicitly modeling anatomical geometry from a single image. We recast the problem as geometry learning of multi-scale structural priors, realized through two synergistic components. First, structured sampling captures the body's geometric continuity through dual-level feature extraction, acquiring both local joint appearance and continuous features along skeletal limbs via deformable sampling. By propagating limb-level geometric cues to their connected joints, this design bridges information gaps caused by occlusion. Second, geometric correction ensures global 3D consistency by lifting coherent 2D features into a canonical 3D reference space, where a shared 3D anchor guides a distance-aware fusion mechanism. Extensive experiments conducted on Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP demonstrate that Glimpse achieves state-of-the-art performance, with superior robustness under severe occlusion and complex articulation.
